Heard instantly while you change it. Changes only the movie sound in your headphones, never the TV.
Starts instantly: the TV shows the picture and the sound plays in your headphones. Turn on Room speakers too if you also want sound from the TV.

YouTube on the TV: open it in TheatreSync (Now casting) and switch on Sound in headphones. The phone plays the same video in step and the TV goes quiet. The headphones you pick here are used for movies and YouTube: they switch the moment you tap them.

Before your movie starts, the TV shows the Quantari Solutions logo with its gold shine and a slowly building glow, then “Presented with TheatreSync · a Quantari Solutions module” (about 6 seconds). Then the film begins, with headphone sound starting exactly with it.
Before movies, YouTube and mirroring started from TheatreSync. Casting from other apps can\'t be changed.
Hear what\'s playing on %1$s in your headphones, in step with the picture. The TV\'s speakers go quiet.
YouTube won\'t play this video outside its own apps, so its sound is back on the TV.

Kept in step with the TV automatically. On other pages the sound link stays as a small tile in the corner (✕ switches it off). Adverts can differ between the TV and the headphones for a moment; it catches up afterwards.
For YouTube, the guest\'s browser plays the same video\'s sound, kept in step with the TV by this phone. Works whoever cast it. Keep TheatreSync running.
Sound link. YouTube needs it on screen to send the sound to your headphones.

Looking for your projector and receiver on the Wi-Fi…
None found on the Wi-Fi yet. In the projector\'s and receiver\'s own menus, switch on network control (often called Network Standby, Network Control, PJLink or IP Control), then tap Search again.

Android plays movie sound on one Bluetooth headset per phone (connecting a second one takes over from the first). For a second pair, pair it with another phone and use TapIn below: same sound, in sync.

Hold their phone to the back of this one

Your phone can send the same sound to several headphones with Bluetooth LE Audio (Auracast). The headphones must support LE Audio / Auracast too. Open Android\'s audio sharing, add the headphones, and everything you play goes to all of them.

Sending the same sound to two headsets needs Bluetooth LE Audio (Auracast) in both the phone and the headphones. This phone doesn\'t report it, so Android plays to one headset at a time. Newer phones and headphones (including some with a firmware update) have it.
For movies this already works with any headphones: each extra pair listens through another phone with TapIn, in sync. No app needed on their phone.

TheatreSync, from Quantari Solutions: movie on the big screen, sound in everyone\'s headphones. Android: open the attached app to install it. iPhone: no install needed, scan or tap the TapIn code on the host\'s phone during a movie.
Nothing queued yet. In a playlist or Mix, the next videos show here.
Tap a video to play it now. Swipe the big picture left for next, right for previous.

Made on this phone from the movie\'s speech; nothing is uploaded. The first time, the language\'s speech pack (40–100 MB) downloads once. A full movie takes a while (once; it\'s saved). Translation downloads that language once.
That file has no subtitles TheatreSync can read (.srt or .vtt).
Subtitles ready. They show from the next start of the movie.
YouTube on the TV: skip ads and sponsor segments

Presses “Skip ad” the moment YouTube allows it, mutes ads that can\'t be skipped (sound returns when the video resumes), and skips sponsor, self-promotion and “like and subscribe” segments using SponsorBlock\'s community database. Works for YouTube on your TVs, cast from any phone.
TheatreSync finds it by itself when it\'s on or in Art mode. If it isn\'t listed, type its address (on the TV: Settings → General → Network → Network Status → IP settings).
You\'re not on this TV\'s Wi-Fi: YouTube goes there over the internet. The TV must be on (on a Chromecast, with YouTube open there).
